This script defines each patient's outcomes and compares the STR and multi-tablet groups, unadjusted and weighted: the analyses behind the paper's Table 3. It adds outcome columns to `patients` and produces `outcome_summary` and `outcome_models`.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/08_outcomes.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/08_outcomes.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/functions.R)

Translated from [`stata/Do Final Analysis.do`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Final%20Analysis.do), lines 56-68, 102-106 and 131-173 and 196-203.

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

## Retention in care

At least two viral loads in days 0-364, more than 90 days apart. Stata needed eleven lines: mark viral load days, blank out the rest, count them, multiply the indicator by the date to get measurement dates, take the minimum and maximum, subtract, and drop the helper variables. Filtering to first-year test days and summarising per patient says it in one step.

```{r}
#| label: define-retention
#| eval: false
```

## Other outcomes

Each `by studyid: egen x = max(...)` or `mean(...)` in Stata becomes one line of a per-patient `summarise()`. `any()` is the R counterpart of `max()` over a 0/1 variable.

Every outcome uses the first year, days 0-364, as the paper describes: the data are filtered to `first_year` before summarising. This is a deliberate departure from the saved Stata. Its `egen` lines for suppression on the initial regimen, days covered and regimen change ran over every one of a patient's days to the end of 2013, so a patient who started in 2008 would contribute up to six years and one who started late in 2011 two, and every day after a patient stopped filling would count as uncovered. The 2015 version of the same code limited the data to the first year first; the saved file lacks that step ([details](stata_overview.qmd#slips-in-the-code)).

```{r}
#| label: define-patient-outcomes
#| eval: false
```

## Odds ratios

For each outcome, one unadjusted and one weighted logistic regression, collected in a table. In Stata each was a pair of lines repeated for every outcome:

```stata
logistic RetainedInCareFirstYear InitialRegimenSTR if FirstObservationOfSubject
logistic RetainedInCareFirstYear InitialRegimenSTR if FirstObservationOfSubject [pw=IPW]
```

A loop over outcome names keeps every result in one table instead of in a log file.

```{r}
#| label: fit-outcome-models
#| eval: false
```
